stem: A and B are brothers. C is the sister of B. D is the mother of A. E is the father of C. How is D related to E?

per_option_rationale.rationale: A and B are brothers. C is B's sister, so C is also a sibling of A. D is A's mother, E is C's father. Since A, B, C are siblings, D and E are their parents: D is E's wife.
Student treats D as a sibling of E rather than tracing that D and E share the same children, placing D at the same generational level as E but in a sibling relation.
Student reverses the direction of the parent-child link, making D a child of E instead of a co-parent.
Student adds an extra generation upward, treating D as E's mother instead of E's wife.

explanation: A and B are brothers, and C is the sister of B, so A, B, C are all siblings. D is the mother of A, so D is the mother of all three siblings. E is the father of C, so E is the father of all three siblings. D and E are parents of the same children, making D the wife of E.

explanation_sections.punchline: A, B, and C are siblings. D is the mother of one sibling and E is the father of another. Since they share the same children, D is E's wife.
explanation_sections.approach: For multi-person blood-relation problems, build the family tree layer by layer. First identify who is in the same generation. Then identify the parents. When two people are parents of the same set of siblings, they are spouses. Do not assume a relation between D and E until you have placed all siblings first.
explanation_sections.lesson: If person D is the mother of a sibling group and person E is the father of the same sibling group, then D and E are husband and wife, not siblings or parent and child.
explanation_sections.timing: About 90 seconds. Identifying that A, B, C are siblings takes 20 seconds. Recognising that D and E share the same children takes another 20 seconds. The remaining time is for selecting and confirming the answer.
